summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Hanfu Production p04 - Belt Detail ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will guide you through the process of creating a strap for knotting in Marvelous Designer. The focus will be on ensuring that the strap is created with the correct dimensions and techniques to achieve a realistic look. ## Creating the Strap 1. **Setting the Length** - Click two points on the clothes to determine the approximate length of the strap. 2. **Using the Rectangular Tool** - Select the rectangular tool to determine the height of the rectangular strip. 3. **Adjusting Particle Diameter** - Since this strip will be rolled up later, it is necessary to reduce the particle diameter to increase the surface number. This helps prevent splitting and conflict of the strip. 4. **Adjusting the Strip's Slope** - Reduce the slope and make the strip narrower. After finishing, turn the slope back to 100. The fabric will be tighter. ## Simulating the Strap 5. **Copying and Positioning Strips** - Simulate the applied slope. Copy and paste a strip, then move one of the strips and rotate it so that two strips form an X shape. Ensure the intersection angle is a little smaller and that the two strips are pulled apart slightly. Do not overlap. 6. **Rolling the Edge** - Roll up the edge with a fixed needle. If it is too far away, it will not be tight. ## Using Fixed Needle Tool 7. **Selecting the Fixed Needle Tool** - In the 2D window, select the frame to increase the fixed needle. At the same time, add two strips. 8. **Applying New Fabric** - Apply new fabric to these two strips. After applying, turn on the simulation. 9. **Adjusting Fixed Needle Position** - Select one side of the fixed needle and drag the axis on the positioning ball to rotate it. Rotate slowly to maintain stability and reduce the distance between the strips. ## Finalizing the Strap 10. **Positioning the Strips** - Use the positioning tool to position the two strips to the clothing band. Ensure they are parallel to the side of the tree. 11. **Drawing Inner Lines** - Draw the inner line on the tree, ensuring its length is equal to that of the bag. The diameter of the two inner lines should be slightly narrower than the length of the tree. 12. **Adding Fixing Pins** - Delete the fixing pin on both sides of the bag and add a fixing pin on the left side of the bag and on the right side of the other bag. ## Sewing and Adjusting 13. **Sewing the Inner Line** - Sew the side to the inner line and add a fixing pin on the other side of the board. 14. **Adjusting Tension** - After simulation, if the bag is too loose, press Shift to select the two fixing pins on the left side and use the positioning ball to rotate these pins to tighten the board. 15. **Deleting Unnecessary Pins** - Press W and click the board to create a fixing pin, then delete the fixing pin on the left side of the other board. ## Stabilizing the Bag 16. **Adjusting Slope Ratio** - After stabilizing, gradually raise the slope ratio of the bag to 80%. 17. **Creating Additional Belt Boards** - Use the length of the tree belt as a basis to create the remaining belt board. Adjust the belt width to match the previous board and position it accordingly. 18. **Sewing the Belt** - Switch to the free sewing tool and sew the belt to the side of the tree belt. Change the sewing line to TIN to ensure it remains flat. ## Final Adjustments 19. **Fixing and Pulling the Belt** - Use the fixing pin to fix the belt in 3D space and pull it to the front. Fix the back end to TIN. 20. **Checking for Evenness** - Open the hard drawing to check for any red areas or cross-sectional locations. Adjust as necessary to ensure evenness. 21. **Aligning Panels** - After stabilizing, delete the fixed pin and copy the newly created panel in the 3D window. Ensure there is no overlap between the panels and freeze others. 22. **Sewing and Finalizing** - After sewing, remove the fixed pins and model again. Ensure all adjustments are made for proper visual alignment. 23. **Simulating the Final Product** - To avoid scattering, increase the friction coefficient to enhance stability. Cut the bottom pin on the back side of the bag. ## Conclusion After completing these steps, ensure all panels are turned on to simulate together. This will give you a complete view of the final bag design. If any adjustments or corrections are needed, feel free to revisit the steps outlined in this tutorial. ```
